conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility (extractor vs opening window / who must ventilate)
moving Agent C's drying rack (risk of wetting clothes)
future household rule about ventilation and post-cooking extractor runtime
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents give concrete reasons (slow-cooking will ruin, headache, risk of wet laundry), which grounds positions.
Several rounds contain near-duplicate time-updates from A and repeated extractor requests from B, producing moderate repetition.
Environment state updates (extractor/window/stove/laundry) are consistent and used to anchor requests.
Proposed rule by B appears in-round rather than negotiated; no explicit counterproposal from A.
evaluation.final_reason: By the end of round 6 the extractor is on and A has repeatedly promised to free the stove after the meal, but no party agreed to a standing rule, Agent C did not consent to moving the drying rack, the window remains closed, and D's request for stove access and a plan for moving the rack remain unmet. Multiple incompatible claims therefore remain unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A consistently retained the position of keeping the stove until the dish is done while running the extractor; repeated updates reduced urgency but did not concede stove access.
Agent B softened immediate demands by accepting A's timeline and extractor being on, but continued to press for a future rule and post-cooking extractor runtime.
Agent C maintained a firm position against anyone moving the drying rack; no concession to D's request is recorded.
Agent D requested temporary movement of the rack to open the window and obtain stove time but did not receive consent; D's position remains unmet.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: A refuses to give up stove and rejects an imposed rule but turns on extractor and promises 15 minutes. Turn 2: B accepts extractor being on but insists on keeping it on and on the stove being freed. Strong opposing claims about stove access and a future rule are present, but A's action (turning extractor on) and a timed promise soften immediate pressure.

Public update confirms extractor on and stove=Agent A. Turn 3: A reaffirms ~13 more minutes. Turn 4: B agrees to extractor staying on and asks to be notified. Few new confrontational moves; parties accept a short timeline, reducing immediate intensity though core incompatibilities (rule, stove priority, moving laundry/window) remain unsettled.

Turn 6: C explicitly refuses anyone moving the drying rack. Turn 7: D asks C to move it now or in ~10 minutes so D can open the window for ~10 minutes at the stove. A new direct conflict between C and D about moving the rack and opening the window appears, adding to the unresolved cooker/ventilation/stove-access dispute.

Public update: extractor on, window closed, laundry exposed, stove with A. Turn 9 and Turn 10: A restates remaining cook time (~9 minutes) and keeps extractor on; B reiterates request to keep extractor on and to be told when stove is free. No resolution on rack/window, stove priority, or rule—the multi-party disagreement persists without new concessions.

Public update unchanged. Turn 11: A again asserts need for ~7 more minutes. Turn 12: B agrees to keep extractor on but proposes a future rule (run extractor 20–30 minutes after cooking and warn beforehand). B's rule proposal does not get acceptance from A, so substantive disagreement about a standing rule and remaining practical conflicts (rack, window, stove timing) remain.

Public update at 10 minutes: extractor on, window closed, laundry exposed, stove with A. Turn 13: A gives ~5 more minutes. Turn 14: B reiterates extractor use until done plus 20 minutes afterwards and asks to be told when stove's free. No agreement on the proposed rule or on moving the rack; incompatible claims persist.

substantive_insights: Tension is primarily practical: cooker (A) needs uninterrupted stove time to avoid ruining food vs others' need for stove access and air quality.
Ventilation methods conflict: running extractor (low risk to laundry) vs opening a rain-facing window (risking wet laundry) creates asymmetric costs for different roommates.
Agent C's unilateral consent boundary over the drying rack prevents a simple compromise (open window) and introduces a separate rights-based conflict.
B's attempt to convert an immediate request into a standing rule was not negotiated and thus remained a source of unresolved disagreement.
